verdicts.note: Attacked on strength, since the statement for calls it restoring 'the levy rate to what it was twenty years ago' (S1). It is still a levy lid lift (S1), the pole_b cap-lift case, raising the rate 17 cents, about 63%, from $0.27 to $0.44 (S1, S2), above the no-vote alternative and not a renewal of an expiring levy. Strength 2 matches Lewis's Timberland lid lift (about 53%). S1 and S2 support the figures. No spending mapping: the stated purpose is restoring hours and staff (S1, S2).

what_it_does matches S1 ($0.27 to $0.44 for 2027 collection; base for later limits under ch. 84.55 RCW; hours, staffing, programs and materials) and the dossier's note that Colville and Kettle Falls are outside the district (S5). The lead verb 'Restores' echoes the statement for; the ballot text calls it a lid lift 'to increase its levy rate', a framing nuance only. cost_line matches S1 ($4.25 a month on a $300,000 home, about $51 a year). pro_summary matches the statement for (S1): authors, 100+ open hours a week, evenings and weekends, $6.2 million borrowed and 'four times the amount collected in taxes', no state or federal operating funds. con_summary matches S1 (no statement against) and S4 (April 2026: 53.85% no to 46.15% yes).

A lid lift from $0.54 to $0.75 per $1,000 (about 39%) that resets the base for later years (S1), not a renewal. Strength 2 is consistent with Whatcom Fire District 1 (about 32%) and Lewis Fire District 6. The stated purpose of maintaining current service (S1) argues against a spending mapping, not against the taxes strength.

what_it_does matches S1 ($0.75 for 2027 collection; equipment, vehicles, stations, trained personnel; Resolution No. 2-2026; base for later limits). cost_line matches S1 (current $0.54; 'an addition $21.00 per year ... per $100,000'). pro_summary correctly says no statement for was filed and quotes the explanatory statement's 'necessary to maintain the current level of fire protection' reasoning (S1); the guide attributes that determination to the Board of Commissioners, so 'the board's explanatory statement' is fair. con_summary matches S1.

Attacked toward 0: the levy continues about $4.4 million a year. A replacement of an expiring EP&O levy at a lower estimated rate ($2.10 against $2.27 in 2026; S1, S2) is the renewal tier other packages score at 1 (Spokane replacement school levies, Benton Ki-Be). Attacked toward 2 and rejected: it is not new or larger. No spending mapping: the con side's spending critique (S1) is opposition argument, not the measure's content.

what_it_does matches S1 (Resolution No. 11-26; expires 2027; 2028-2030; listed uses). cost_line matches the ballot-title table (S1). pro_summary: no statement for and the committee are as S1 lists; '17% of the budget' is Baerwald per S2. 'The district is lowering the rate' is supported by S2's rate comparison ($2.10 against $2.27; combined $2.48 against $2.65) as a district estimate, but the dossier does not put those words in Baerwald's mouth, a minor attribution looseness not worth a correction. con_summary matches the statement against (S1): authors, 90 days, 'not funded by the State', 50th in income and 235th in dollars per student (the committee's figures, unchecked per the dossier). 'A district levy' rejected 90 days earlier was the separate April capital levy (S3, S4); the wording is accurate.

Attacked toward 2. The ballot title does not call it a replacement (S1), the Spokesman-Review calls it 'a new tax' offset by the expiring bond (S2), and the bond ends at the end of 2026 whatever the vote (S1, S2), so against the no-vote alternative a yes vote adds about $4.85 million over six years. But the measure holds the district's rate at the same 38 cents rather than raising it (S1, S2), and the district's combined rate falls from $2.65 to $2.48 if both pass (S2). Treating a same-rate bond-to-levy swap as the renewal tier (1) is defensible and consistent with how other packages score same-rate replacements. The basis states the legal-novelty caveat openly.

what_it_does matches the ballot title (S1): six-year capital levy 2027-2032, Resolution No. 12-26, failing roof and 'condemned portable classrooms' at Lakeside High School, district-wide security, fire systems, facilities and infrastructure. cost_line matches S1 ($0.38; $774,853 in 2027 to $842,954 in 2032) and the statement for's bond expiring January 1, 2027 (S1). pro_summary matches the statement for (S1): authors, same-rate replacement of the expiring bond, projects cut after tax concerns, roof, condemned classrooms, fire and camera systems. con_summary matches the statement against and rebuttal (S1): 90 days, 'far more vague about projects', 'carte blanche', 'budgets for recovering these sunk costs' (election costs), portables not 'essential'.
